section: Part 1 — Scope and Definitions / 1.1 Purpose of the Program
text:
The Household Support Program provides monthly financial assistance to
qualifying households in Calder County to meet essential living costs, together with
access to associated support services.

section: Part 1 — Scope and Definitions / 1.1 Purpose of the Program
text:
The Program is administered by the Calder County Department of Household
Services ("the Department"). Day-to-day administration is carried out by caseworkers at
the four district offices.

section: Part 1 — Scope and Definitions / 1.1 Purpose of the Program
text:
Nothing in this manual creates an entitlement beyond that established by the
governing statute. Where a provision of this manual confers discretion on the Department, that discretion must be exercised reasonably and the reasons recorded on
the case file.

section: Part 1 — Scope and Definitions / 1.2 Structure of this manual
text:
This manual is divided into twelve parts. Parts 1 to 5 address eligibility. Parts 6
and 7 address the calculation of the award. Parts 8 to 10 address the ongoing
administration of a claim, including changes of circumstance, overpayments, and
recovery. Parts 11 and 12 address review and appeal.

section: Part 1 — Scope and Definitions / 1.2 Structure of this manual
text:
Cross-references in this manual are given in the form §4.3.2, referring to Part
4, section 3, paragraph 2.

section: Part 1 — Scope and Definitions / 1.2 Structure of this manual
text:
This manual is amended by numbered amendment. Each amendment states
its own effective date. Where an amendment is in force, the amended text applies to
determinations made on or after the effective date of the amendment, except where the
amendment provides otherwise.

section: Part 1 — Scope and Definitions / 1.3 Interpretation
text:
In this manual, "must" indicates a mandatory requirement, "may" indicates a
discretion, and "should" indicates the ordinary expected practice from which a
caseworker may depart where the case file records the reason.

section: Part 1 — Scope and Definitions / 1.3 Interpretation
text:
A period expressed in days means calendar days unless the provision states
otherwise. Where the last day of a period falls on a day on which the district office is
closed, the period ends on the next day on which the office is open.

section: Part 1 — Scope and Definitions / 1.3 Interpretation
text:
References to a monetary amount are to the amount in force at the date of the
determination.


**1.4.1 Applicant** — a person who has submitted an application for assistance under
the Program and whose application has not yet been determined.

**1.4.2 Recipient** — a person in receipt of assistance under the Program.

**1.4.3 Household** — the applicant or recipient together with every other person who
ordinarily resides at the same address and who shares living arrangements with the
applicant or recipient. Persons sharing an address under a separate tenancy or licence,
and having no shared living arrangements, are not members of the household.

**1.4.4 Household member** — any person falling within §1.4.3 other than the
applicant or recipient.

**1.4.5 Dependent child** — a person under the age of 18 who is a household
member, or a person aged 18 to 20 who is a household member and is enrolled in
secondary education.

**1.4.6 Full-time student** — a person enrolled in a course of study at an accredited
institution of higher education, where the institution classifies the enrolment as fulltime. Enrolment status is determined by reference to the institution's own classification
and not by the number of contact hours.

**1.4.7 Countable income** — income falling within Part 6 that is not disregarded
under §6.4.

**1.4.8 Change of circumstances** — any change in the facts on which a
determination of eligibility or award was based, including a change in household
composition, income, address, or the circumstances of any household member.

**1.4.9 Determination** — a decision by the Department on entitlement, amount,
suspension, or termination.

**1.4.10 District office** — any of the four offices of the Department at Calder Central,
Northgate, Weybridge, and Ash Hill.

**1.4.11 Working day** — a day on which the district office is open to the public.

section: Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.1 The basic conditions
text:
A person is eligible for assistance under the Program if, at the date of
determination, that person satisfies each of the conditions in §2.1.2.

section: Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.1 The basic conditions
Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.1 The basic conditions
text:
Eligibility is assessed at the level of the household. Where more than one
member of a household would independently qualify, one application is made on behalf
of the household and one award is made.

section: Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.2 Continuing eligibility
text:
Eligibility must be satisfied throughout the period of the award. A recipient
who ceases to satisfy any condition in §2.1.2 ceases to be eligible from the date the
condition ceased to be satisfied.

section: Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.2 Continuing eligibility
text:
The Department reviews each award at intervals not exceeding twelve
months. A review is not a fresh application and does not require the recipient to reestablish matters already determined, unless there has been a change of
circumstances affecting those matters.

section: Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.3 Applicants under 18
text:
A person aged 16 or 17 may be eligible where that person —
(a) is not a household member of any other household; and
(b) has no person with parental responsibility able and willing to provide support; or
(c) is a parent of a dependent child residing with them.

section: Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.3 Applicants under 18
text:
An application under §2.3.1 must be referred to a supervisor before
determination.

section: Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.4 Resources
text:
A household is not eligible where the total countable resources of the
household exceed $4,000.

section: Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.4 Resources
Part 2 — General Conditions of Eligibility / 2.4 Resources
text:
Resources held jointly with a person who is not a household member are
countable in proportion to the recipient's beneficial interest. Where the proportion
cannot be established, an equal division is presumed.

section: Part 3 — Residence / 3.1 The residence condition
text:
An applicant satisfies the residence condition where the applicant ordinarily
resides at an address in Calder County and intends to continue to do so.

section: Part 3 — Residence / 3.1 The residence condition
text:
Ordinary residence is a question of fact. Physical presence on the date of
application is neither necessary nor sufficient.

section: Part 3 — Residence / 3.1 The residence condition
text:
An applicant who has no fixed address but whose connection to the County is
established under §3.3 satisfies the residence condition.

section: Part 3 — Residence / 3.2 Temporary absence from the County
text:
A recipient who is temporarily absent from Calder County continues to satisfy
the residence condition for the first 28 days of the absence.

section: Part 3 — Residence / 3.2 Temporary absence from the County
text:
The period in §3.2.1 is extended to 90 days where the absence is for the
purpose of —
(a) receiving medical treatment that is not available within the County;
(b) accompanying a household member receiving such treatment; or
(c) attending to the affairs of a deceased relative.

section: Part 3 — Residence / 3.2 Temporary absence from the County
text:
Temporary absence does not include absence for the purpose of full-time
education, which is addressed separately.

section: Part 3 — Residence / 3.2 Temporary absence from the County
text:
An absence exceeding the applicable period ends eligibility from the first day
following the expiry of that period, unless the Department is satisfied that the recipient
intended throughout to return and that the extension of the absence was outside the
recipient's control.

section: Part 3 — Residence / 3.3 Applicants with no fixed address
text:
Where an applicant has no fixed address, connection to the County may be
established by —
(a) a period of at least 30 days spent in the County immediately before application;
(b) registration with a general practitioner, shelter, or day service in the County; or
(c) confirmation from a recognised support agency operating in the County.

section: Part 3 — Residence / 3.3 Applicants with no fixed address
text:
Correspondence for an applicant with no fixed address may be directed to a
district office and held for collection. The Department must record the arrangement on
the case file and must not treat non-collection of correspondence as a failure to
respond for the purposes of §8.6.

section: Part 4 — Exclusions / 4.1 Excluded persons
text:
A person is excluded from eligibility where that person —
(a) is subject to an unexpired sanction under §10.5;
(b) is detained in a correctional facility;
(c) is in receipt of assistance from an equivalent program administered by another
county or state; or
(d) has been determined under §9.6 to have obtained assistance by deliberate
misrepresentation, for the period stated in that determination.

section: Part 4 — Exclusions / 4.1 Excluded persons
text:
Exclusion of one household member does not exclude the household. Where
a household member is excluded, that member's needs are removed from the
calculation under Part 7 but that member's income remains countable under Part 6.

section: Part 4 — Exclusions / 4.2 Persons in residential care
text:
A person residing in a residential care facility is not a member of the
household of which they were previously a member, from the date the residence
becomes permanent.

section: Part 4 — Exclusions / 4.2 Persons in residential care
text:
Residence in a residential care facility is treated as temporary for the first 56
days.

section: Part 4 — Exclusions / 4.3 Recipient obligations
Part 4 — Exclusions / 4.3 Recipient obligations
text:
A recipient must report any change in household composition, income,
address, or the circumstances of any household member within **10 calendar days**
of the change occurring, or within 10 calendar days of the recipient becoming aware of
the change, whichever is later.

section: Part 4 — Exclusions / 4.3 Recipient obligations
text:
A report under §4.3.2 may be made in person at a district office, by telephone
to the Program line, in writing, or through the online account. The date of report is the
date the report is received by the Department, regardless of the method used.

section: Part 4 — Exclusions / 4.3 Recipient obligations
text:
Failure to report within the period in §4.3.2 may result in a sanction under
§10.5 and may result in an overpayment recoverable under Part 9.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.1 Households including a person in residential care
text:
Where a household member enters residential care, the award is recalculated
from the date the residence is treated as permanent under §4.2.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.1 Households including a person in residential care
text:
During the period in which the residence is treated as temporary, the award is
unchanged.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.2 Households including a temporarily absent member
text:
A household member who is temporarily absent from the household address
remains a household member for the first 28 days of the absence.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.2 Households including a temporarily absent member
text:
The period in §5.2.1 is extended to 90 days where the absence is for a reason
listed in §3.2.2.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.2 Households including a temporarily absent member
text:
Temporary absence does not include absence for the purpose of full-time
education, which is addressed separately.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.3 Households including a person receiving a training allowance
text:
Where a household member is in receipt of a training allowance under a
recognised employment program, that allowance is disregarded in full under §6.4.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.3 Households including a person receiving a training allowance
text:
A household member in receipt of a training allowance remains a household
member for all purposes of this manual.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.4 Households including a person in receipt of a care allowance
text:
Where a household member is in receipt of a care allowance in respect of the
care of another household member, the allowance is disregarded to the extent set out in
§6.4.1(f).

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.4 Households including a person in receipt of a care allowance
text:
The presence of a care allowance does not of itself alter the composition of
the household.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.5 Households with a member subject to immigration conditions
text:
Where a household member is subject to a condition prohibiting recourse to
public assistance, that member's needs are excluded from the calculation under Part 7
and that member's income is disregarded.

section: Part 5 — Special Household Circumstances / 5.5 Households with a member subject to immigration conditions
text:
A case falling within §5.5.1 must be referred to a supervisor before
determination.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.1 General
text:
The countable income of a household is the total income of every household
member, less the disregards in §6.4.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.1 General
text:
Income is counted in the period in which it is received, except where §6.3
applies.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.2 Income that is counted
Part 6 — Income / 6.3 Irregular and lump-sum income
text:
A lump sum received by a household member is treated as a resource under
§2.4 from the date of receipt, and is not counted as income, except where §6.3.2
applies.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.3 Irregular and lump-sum income
text:
Where a lump sum represents arrears of income that would have been
counted had it been paid when due, it is counted as income and attributed to the period
to which it relates.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.3 Irregular and lump-sum income
text:
Irregular earnings are averaged over the thirteen weeks preceding the
determination, or over such shorter period as gives a fair reflection of the household's
circumstances.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.4 Disregards
Part 6 — Income / 6.4 Disregards
text:
The disregard in §6.4.1(a) applies once per household and not once per
earner.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.5 Self-employment
text:
Net profit is gross receipts less expenses wholly and necessarily incurred in
the business.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.5 Self-employment
text:
The following are not allowable expenses — capital expenditure, depreciation,
entertainment, and any payment to a household member.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.5 Self-employment
text:
Where self-employment has been carried on for less than thirteen weeks, the
Department may estimate net profit on the basis of the trading to date.

section: Part 6 — Income / 6.6 Income thresholds
text:
A household is not eligible where countable income exceeds the applicable
threshold. The thresholds are —

| Household size | Monthly threshold |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | $1,180 |
| 2 | $1,590 |
| 3 | $2,000 |
| 4 | $2,410 |
| 5 | $2,820 |
| each additional member | + $410 |

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.1 The award
text:
The monthly award is the applicable needs figure for the household under
§7.2, less countable income.

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.1 The award
text: Where the resulting figure is less than $25, no award is made.

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.1 The award
text:
The needs figure is calculated by reference to household size and
composition, except in the case of full-time students (see §5.4), and is subject to the
adjustments in §7.3.

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.2 Needs figures
text:
The monthly needs figures are —

| Household composition | Monthly needs figure |
|:--|:--|
| Single adult | $1,240 |
| Couple | $1,670 |
| Each dependent child | + $330 |
| Single adult with one or more dependent children | $1,480 base |

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.2 Needs figures
text:
A household member who is excluded under Part 4 is not counted for the
purposes of §7.2.1.

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.3 Adjustments
text:
The needs figure is increased by $90 per month where a household member
has been assessed as requiring assistance with two or more activities of daily living.

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.3 Adjustments
text:
The needs figure is increased by $140 per month where the household
includes a dependent child under the age of 2.

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.3 Adjustments
text:
The needs figure is reduced by the amount of any housing assistance received
by the household from another program, to the extent that assistance is intended to
meet costs included in the needs figure.

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.4 Payment
text:
Payment is made monthly in arrears, on the day of the month corresponding
to the date of the original determination.

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.4 Payment
text:
Payment is made by direct transfer to a nominated account. Where the
recipient has no account, payment may be made by prepaid card.

section: Part 7 — Calculation of the Award / 7.4 Payment
text:
An award of less than one month's duration is apportioned by reference to the
number of days.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.1 Making an application
text:
An application may be made online, in person at a district office, by
telephone, or in writing.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.1 Making an application
text:
An application is valid where it contains the name and address of the
applicant, the composition of the household, and a signature or its electronic
equivalent.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.1 Making an application
text:
The date of application is the date on which a valid application is received by
the Department. Where an incomplete application is received and subsequently
completed within 30 days, the date of application is the date the incomplete application
was received.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.2 Evidence
text:
An applicant must provide evidence of identity, residence, income, and
resources.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.2 Evidence
text:
Where an applicant is unable to provide a specified document, the
Department must consider alternative evidence and must not refuse an application
solely on the ground that a particular document has not been supplied.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.2 Evidence
text:
The Department must give an applicant at least 14 days to supply requested
evidence, and must extend that period on request where the applicant is taking
reasonable steps to obtain it.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.3 Time limits for determination
text:
The Department must determine an application within 30 days of the date of
application.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.3 Time limits for determination
text:
Where the Department is unable to determine within that period because
evidence remains outstanding, the Department must notify the applicant in writing before the expiry of the period, stating what remains outstanding and the date by which
it is required.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.3 Time limits for determination
text:
An application on which no determination has been made within 90 days of
the date of application must be referred to a supervisor.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.4 Interim payments
text:
Where an application has not been determined within 30 days and the delay is
not attributable to the applicant, the Department may make an interim payment.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.4 Interim payments
text:
An interim payment is recoverable against the eventual award and, where the
application is refused, is recoverable under Part 9 only where the applicant provided
information that was materially false.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.5 Interviews
text:
The Department may require an applicant or recipient to attend an interview
at a district office where —
(a) the information provided is incomplete or inconsistent;
(b) the case has been selected for review under §2.2.2; or
(c) a change of circumstances has been reported that materially affects the award.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.5 Interviews
text:
At least 10 days' notice of an interview must be given, and the notice must
state the purpose of the interview.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.5 Interviews
text:
An applicant or recipient may be accompanied at an interview by a person of
their choosing.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.6 Failure to respond
text:
Where an applicant fails without good cause to provide requested evidence
within the period allowed, the application may be refused.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.6 Failure to respond
text:
Where a recipient fails without good cause to provide requested evidence
within the period allowed, the award may be suspended under §10.2.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.6 Failure to respond
text:
Before refusing or suspending under this section, the Department must make
at least two attempts to contact the person, using at least two different methods, and
must record those attempts on the case file.

section: Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.7 Notification of determinations
Part 8 — Applications and Determinations / 8.7 Notification of determinations
text: A determination takes effect from the date stated in the notification.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.1 Establishing an overpayment
text:
An overpayment arises where assistance has been paid to which the recipient
was not entitled.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.1 Establishing an overpayment
Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.1 Establishing an overpayment
text:
The Department must determine the period and amount of the overpayment
and must notify the recipient under §8.7.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.1 Establishing an overpayment
text:
Where an overpayment has arisen from a change of circumstances, and the
recipient reported the change within the **30 calendar days** required under §4.3, no
overpayment shall be established in respect of any period before the date on which the
Department was in a position to act on the report.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.1 Establishing an overpayment
text:
An overpayment arising solely from an error by the Department, where the
recipient could not reasonably have been expected to know that the payment was
incorrect, is not recoverable.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.2 Amount recoverable
text:
The amount recoverable is the difference between the assistance paid and
the assistance that would have been paid had the correct facts been known.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.2 Amount recoverable
text:
In calculating the amount recoverable, the Department must apply any
income or needs adjustment that would have applied over the same period, whether
that adjustment increases or reduces the amount.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.3 Recovery
text:
Recovery may be made by deduction from ongoing assistance, by agreed
instalments, or by any other lawful means.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.3 Recovery
text:
Deduction from ongoing assistance must not exceed 10 per cent of the
monthly award, or 20 per cent where §9.6 applies.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.3 Recovery
text:
The Department must consider the recipient's circumstances before setting a
rate of recovery and must reduce the rate on request where recovery at the standard
rate would cause hardship.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.4 Waiver
text:
The Department may waive recovery in whole or in part where —
(a) recovery would cause serious hardship;
(b) the cost of recovery would exceed the amount recoverable; or
(c) the overpayment arose from Departmental error and recovery would be inequitable.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.4 Waiver
text: A decision on waiver must be recorded with reasons.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.5 Time limits
text:
No overpayment may be established more than 6 years after the date of the
last payment to which it relates.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.5 Time limits
text: There is no time limit on recovery of an overpayment once established.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.6 Deliberate misrepresentation
text:
Where the Department determines that a recipient deliberately
misrepresented or deliberately failed to disclose a material fact, the Department may —
(a) recover at the higher rate under §9.3.2; and
(b) exclude the person from eligibility under §4.1.1(d) for a period not exceeding 13
weeks for a first determination, or 26 weeks for a subsequent determination.

section: Part 9 — Overpayments and Recovery / 9.6 Deliberate misrepresentation
text:
A determination under §9.6.1 must be made by a supervisor and must be
based on evidence recorded on the case file. A failure to report, without more, is not
evidence of deliberate misrepresentation.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.1 Termination
text:
An award terminates where the recipient ceases to satisfy any condition in
§2.1.2, from the date the condition ceased to be satisfied.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.1 Termination
text:
An award terminates on the death of the recipient. Where the household
includes surviving members, a fresh application may be made and, if made within 30
days, the date of application is treated as the date of death.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.2 Suspension
text:
The Department may suspend an award where —
(a) the recipient has failed to respond under §8.6.2;
(b) there is reason to believe the recipient may no longer be eligible and the matter
cannot be determined immediately; or
(c) the recipient's whereabouts are unknown.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.2 Suspension
text:
A suspension must be notified under §8.7 and must state what the recipient
must do for the award to be reinstated.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.2 Suspension
text:
A suspension that has continued for 60 days without resolution must be
referred to a supervisor for a determination on termination.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.2 Suspension
text:
Where a suspension is lifted, arrears are paid for the whole period of
suspension where the recipient was eligible throughout.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.3 Reinstatement
text: An award terminated in error is reinstated from the date of termination.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.3 Reinstatement
text:
Where an award was terminated because a condition ceased to be satisfied,
and that condition is satisfied again within 30 days, the recipient may request
reinstatement rather than making a fresh application.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.4 Effect on the household
text:
Suspension or termination in respect of one household member does not of
itself affect the eligibility of the household.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.5 Sanctions
text:
The Department may impose a sanction where a recipient, without good
cause —
(a) fails to report a change of circumstances within the period required by §4.3.2;
(b) fails to attend an interview required under §8.5; or
(c) fails to comply with a condition attached to the award.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.5 Sanctions
text:
A sanction is a reduction of the monthly award by 20 per cent for a period of
4 weeks for a first sanction, or 8 weeks for a subsequent sanction within 12 months.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.5 Sanctions
text:
A sanction must not be imposed where the household includes a dependent
child under the age of 2, or where the recipient has been assessed as requiring
assistance with two or more activities of daily living.

section: Part 10 — Suspension, Termination and Sanctions / 10.5 Sanctions
text:
Good cause includes illness, a family emergency, a failure of the
Department's own systems, and any circumstance that a reasonable person would
regard as preventing compliance.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.1 Right to review
text:
A person affected by a determination may request a review of that
determination.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.1 Right to review
text:
A request for review must be made within 30 days of the date of the
notification under §8.7. The Department may extend that period where there is good
cause for the delay.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.1 Right to review
text:
A request for review may be made in any form, including orally. The
Department must record the request and must not require it to be made on a particular
form.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.2 Conduct of the review
text:
A review must be carried out by an officer who was not involved in the
original determination.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.2 Conduct of the review
text:
The reviewing officer must consider the whole determination and is not
limited to the matters raised by the person requesting the review.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.2 Conduct of the review
text: A review must be completed within 30 days of the request.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.3 Outcome
text: The reviewing officer may confirm, vary, or set aside the determination.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.3 Outcome
text:
The outcome must be notified under §8.7 and must state the right of appeal
under Part 12.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.4 Payment pending review
text:
Where a review concerns a termination or reduction of an award, the
Department may continue payment at the previous rate pending the outcome.

section: Part 11 — Review / 11.4 Payment pending review
text:
Payment continued under §11.4.1 that proves not to have been due is
recoverable under Part 9, unless the Department determines otherwise.

section: Part 12 — Appeal / 12.1 Right of appeal
text:
A person who has requested a review and is dissatisfied with the outcome
may appeal to the Calder County Assistance Appeals Panel.

section: Part 12 — Appeal / 12.1 Right of appeal
text:
An appeal must be lodged within 30 days of the date of the notification of the
review outcome.

section: Part 12 — Appeal / 12.1 Right of appeal
text:
An appeal may not be lodged until a review has been completed, except
where the Department has failed to complete the review within the period in §11.2.3.

section: Part 12 — Appeal / 12.2 Procedure
text:
The Panel determines its own procedure, subject to the requirements of
fairness.

section: Part 12 — Appeal / 12.2 Procedure
text:
The appellant may appear in person, may be represented, and may call
evidence.

section: Part 12 — Appeal / 12.2 Procedure
text:
The Department must provide the Panel and the appellant with the case file
and a written submission at least 10 days before the hearing.

section: Part 12 — Appeal / 12.3 Decisions of the Panel
text: A decision of the Panel is binding on the Department.

section: Part 12 — Appeal / 12.3 Decisions of the Panel
text: The Panel must give reasons in writing within 14 days of the hearing.

section: Part 12 — Appeal / 12.3 Decisions of the Panel
text:
The Department must give effect to a decision of the Panel within 14 days of
receiving it.

*End of consolidated text as at 31 December 2025.*
